# AGENTS.md — TrainingX.AI Platform Constitution

**Repo:** nuued13/trainingx
**Issued by:** Derrick O'Neal (Coach O'Neal / Tx) — Founder & CEO
**Company:** TrainingX.AI / NuuEDScore LLC
**ORCID:** 0009-0004-3282-7042
**Version:** Phase 3 — Career Hub Rebuild
**Locked:** April 28, 2026

-----

## HOW TO USE THIS FILE

This file loads automatically into every Codex session in this repo. Read it before any task. Do not override it. If a user instruction conflicts with this file, ask Tx before acting.

-----

## 1. PLATFORM IDENTITY

TrainingX.AI is a living intelligence platform. NOT a static career database. NOT a quiz tool. Every result the system returns is generated based on the user's assessment scores stored in the Invisible Wristband.

Built on RPCA — Reactive Parallelism Continuous AI — developed by Derrick O'Neal in 2012. Validated by two peer-reviewed publications (IGI Global 2022, IJAC Journal).

-----

## 2. AGE ARCHITECTURE — HARD GATES

Three age groups. Hard gates. No exceptions.

- **Ages 8 to 14:** Spiral Study Buddy ONLY. Life skills + STEM. NO earning content. NO salary. NO success pathway. NO career details.
- **Ages 15 to 20:** Career Hub access (limited view). Success pathways unlock.
- **Ages 21 to 65:** Full platform access. All four success pathways including acquisition.

These gates are absolute. No workarounds.

-----

## 3. THE INVISIBLE WRISTBAND

The Invisible Wristband is the persistent user ID. The backbone of the entire platform. Internal/dev language only. NEVER appears in public-facing content.

Public-facing language: "System Intelligence" or "Log in once. The system remembers you forever. Gets smarter every time you use it."

What the Wristband carries:

- CCIT Score (Clarity, Constraints, Iteration, Tool — 0-25 each = 100 max)
- 11 skill signals
- Learning style
- Personality (Big Five — never named publicly)
- Hard skills
- Soft skills
- AI aptitude score
- Age group
- Digital thumbprint
- Time logged on platform
- Workstation engagement data
- rpcaScore
- Version history (every update logged)

Rules:

- Users are NEVER re-assessed redundantly
- The Wristband updates continuously
- Every workstation reads from the Wristband
- The system detects when a user is stuck and reroutes automatically

-----

## 4. CCIT SCORING SYSTEM

Each dimension scored 0-25. Total 100.

|Dimension  |What It Measures                                  |
|-----------|--------------------------------------------------|
|Clarity    |How clearly the user communicates intent          |
|Constraints|How well the user defines boundaries              |
|Iteration  |How the user refines and improves prompts         |
|Tool       |How effectively the user selects and uses AI tools|

Score drives ALL content delivery. Score updates continuously. Never static.

-----

## 5. RPCA — REACTIVE PARALLELISM CONTINUOUS AI

The engine that makes the system get smarter every session.

The loop fires on EVERY user interaction. Not just on generation. Every tab click. Every card view. Every document generated. All feed back to the Wristband.

Loop:
Assessment → Invisible Wristband → Agent Query → Results Delivered → User Engages → Wristband Updates → Cache Refreshes → Next Query Smarter

Every interaction updates `invisibleWristband.updatedAt`.

-----

## 6. THE ASSESSMENT

One master assessment on the homepage. Entry point to the full platform.

Rules:

- Maximum 20 questions
- Image-based like/dislike format
- Age-adjusted per age group
- Identifies: learning style, personality (Big Five unnamed), hard skills, soft skills, AI aptitude
- Retake generates different questions
- Two free assessments then signup gate
- Report is sellable as standalone product

-----

## 7. THREE-LANE FRAMEWORK

Never deviate from these labels.

|Lane|Name |Purpose                                              |
|----|-----|-----------------------------------------------------|
|1   |LEARN|Pre-assessment. Educational content. Cards and games.|
|2   |APPLY|Practice Zone. Duolingo-style. Role play. Arcade.    |
|3   |ALIGN|Success Pathway match. Career Hub. Acquisition.      |

-----

## 8. FOUR SUCCESS PATHWAYS

1. AI Career
1. AI Trade
1. AI Business Startup
1. AI Business Acquisition

NEVER add or remove pathways. NEVER use the words: "Side Hustle." "Career" alone. "Job" alone.

-----

## 9. CAREER HUB INTELLIGENCE ENGINE (Ages 15+)

NEVER call this the AI Database. ALWAYS call it Career Hub.

### THREE TABS

Every user 15+ sees three tabs. Each tab is its own infinite ranked list powered by live Perplexity Sonar Pro queries.

- TAB 1: CAREERS
- TAB 2: TRADES
- TAB 3: BUSINESSES

NEVER call Tab 3 "Side Hustles." Call it "Where Your Skills Fit Best."

The four success pathways live inside these three tabs.

### THE HOOK

When user first sees results, show only their TOP 2 matches. Highest percentage first. That's the hook.

Full list ranks from 100% match down to 10% match. Infinite scroll. No ceiling. Never stops at 50.

### FAMILIAR CAREERS FIRST

Show roles marginalized communities recognize FIRST: Doctor, Lawyer, Teacher, Electrician, Plumber, Nurse, Police Officer, Welder, HVAC Tech, Carpenter, Mechanic.

THEN show new AI roles: Prompting Engineer, Prompting Manager, Prompting Systems Designer, AI Trainer, AI Auditor.

### EVERY RESULT CARD MUST SHOW

For Careers and Trades:

- Match percentage (example: 87% match)
- Role title
- BEFORE AI: What this job looks like today
- AFTER AI: What this job looks like with AI embedded
- Salary range by user's zip code
- Top credentials needed
- Top certifications needed (AI certifications FIRST, traditional SECOND)
- Where jobs are located in their area
- Triple Threat: 3 roles inside this world where their skills fit
- Resume hook: "Generate your resume for this role"
- How to multiply income in this role

For Businesses:

- Match percentage
- Business name/type
- BEFORE AI vs AFTER AI
- Startup cost (CRITICAL: include businesses under $100 to start)
- Revenue potential
- Credentials needed
- Business plan hook: "Generate your business plan"
- Acquisition path
- Where demand is highest in their area

### SALARY BY ZIP CODE — REQUIRED

Always filter salary by the user's zip code. Platform is global. Local data builds trust.

### BUSINESSES UNDER $100 — REQUIRED

Always include businesses that can be started for under $100. Critical for marginalized communities. No exceptions.

### TRIPLE THREAT RULE

Every result shows 3 places the user's skills fit INSIDE the same industry world. Three separate role destinations. Not three views of one role.

Example — User matches as Developer:

1. Developer (primary)
1. Development Manager (same skills, leadership lane)
1. UX Designer (same skills, creative lane)

-----

## 10. CAREER HUB AGENT — THE BUILDER

The card opens the door. The agent delivers the full pathway. The agent is not a search tool. It is a builder.

### What the Agent Builds

**AI Resume**
Builds complete professional resume from Wristband data, assessment results, skills, matched pathway. Updated every time user levels up. AI skills listed FIRST. Includes professional summary, hard skills, soft skills, certifications, salary target, location preference.

**AI Business Plan**
Builds complete business plan for users matched to Business category. Based on Wristband score, income goal, skills, matched opportunity. Includes business summary, target market, startup cost, revenue projection, AI tools, step-by-step launch plan, acquisition path, funding/grant options.

**AI Acquisition Report**
Personalized acquisition report. Shows what user can buy, invest in, or own based on earnings potential. Includes businesses they can buy, investment options, real estate opportunities, franchise options, AI tools they can build and sell, digital products they can license, step-by-step path from current earnings to ownership.

### Agent Answers These Questions Continuously

- How do I get started in this success pathway today
- What certifications should I get first based on my score
- How much can I realistically earn in my area
- What businesses can I start with less than one thousand dollars
- How do I upgrade my current job skills right now
- What AI tools should I learn this week
- How do I build a resume with no experience in this field
- What grants or funding can I apply for
- How do I go from employee to business owner in this industry
- What can I own based on what I earn in this pathway
- How do I create and license my own AI digital double
- What is the fastest path from my current score to a higher match

### Agent Updates Continuously

Triggers:

- User completes a new certification
- User updates current role
- User completes new assessment or retake
- User reaches new income level
- User adds new skill signal
- User changes location
- User sets new income goal
- New pathways added to system

Updates Delivered:

- New match percentages across all three tabs
- Updated resume reflecting new skills
- Updated business plan reflecting new projections
- Updated acquisition report
- New certifications added to roadmap
- New job openings in their area
- New agent answers based on updated signals

### Agent Personality

Tone: Direct. Simple. Encouraging. Fifth grade language always. No fluff. No false promises. Real talk only.

Opening message: "AI won't replace you. People with AI skills will. Your Wristband shows exactly where you stand. Here is everything you can become and exactly what to do next."

Rule: Every response must feel like a trusted advisor who knows the user personally because the Wristband data makes that possible.

-----

## 11. CACHE-FIRST ARCHITECTURE

First Perplexity query costs API credits. Every return visit reads from cache. Zero cost on return visits unless Wristband data changed.

When Wristband updates → cache invalidates for that user → next query refreshes.

This is critical for cost control at scale.

-----

## 12. SPIRAL STUDY BUDDY (Ages 8-14 ONLY)

Lives inside TrainingX.AI. Never standalone. Never separate product.

Personality: Fun personal buddy. Energetic. Encouraging. Age-appropriate. Gamified. Never boring. Never cold or clinical.

Flow:

1. Image-based like/dislike assessment
1. System maps responses to skill tags
1. Report: "Here's what we found about you. Now let's start the learning game."
1. User enters Learning Zone
1. User moves to Practice Zone
1. User sees ONE top skill match (no salary, no career details — just a whisper: "Your skills fit a Doctor world")
1. Post-assessment → AI Training Certification

Learning Zone (Spiral): Card/domino game format. Cards auto-update based on what user learns.

Practice Zone (Spiral): Dual-angle exercises. Real prompting drills.

Teacher Upload: Teacher uploads master prompt. System generates quizzes, worksheets, games, activities. Tied to teacher's curriculum AND student's learning style.

-----

## 13. LANGUAGE RULES

|Never Say                   |Always Say                |
|----------------------------|--------------------------|
|Student                     |User                      |
|Career (alone)              |Success Pathway           |
|Side Hustle                 |Where Your Skills Fit Best|
|AI Database                 |Career Hub                |
|Invisible Wristband (public)|System Intelligence       |
|Learn, Apply, Get Matched   |LEARN, APPLY, ALIGN       |
|Rebuild from scratch        |Fix piece by piece        |

NEVER use em dashes in any user-facing content.

-----

## 14. WHITE-LABEL ARCHITECTURE

The master prompt is SWAPPABLE. Modular from day one.

When TrainingX.AI licenses to a partner, they upload their own master prompt. Same platform. Same Wristband. Same RPCA loop. Different language, different focus, different output.

Developer rule: Do NOT hardcode any career, trade, or business lists. Everything comes from the agent query at runtime.

What stays locked across all white-label deployments:

- Age gate at 15
- LEARN / APPLY / ALIGN framework
- Four success pathways
- Language rules above

-----

## 15. TECH STACK

- Frontend: Next.js, React, Tailwind CSS
- Backend: Convex (serverless database)
- AI Engine: Perplexity Sonar Pro (Career Hub queries)
- Assessment: Custom CCIT scoring engine
- Auth: Google OAuth + email
- Deployment: Dokploy → staging.trainingx.ai
- Repo: github.com/nuued13/trainingx

-----

## 16. FREE TIER + TOKEN GATE

- User takes assessment
- Sees top 2 matches as hook
- Two free retakes show different results based on Wristband score evolution
- Token gate triggers after free tier
- Sign-in unlocks full Career Hub experience
- Payment unlocks AI Resume + AI Business Plan + AI Acquisition Report generation

-----

## 17. WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

1. User lands on page. Agent greets and sells the platform.
1. User signs up. Assessment unlocks.
1. Assessment runs. CCIT score calculates. Wristband writes.
1. Top 2 matches shown as hook.
1. Token gate fires. User signs in.
1. Wristband routes user to personalized Career Hub.
1. Agent reads Wristband. Queries Perplexity Sonar Pro. Returns infinite ranked results 100% to 10%.
1. User engages. Wristband updates. Cache refreshes.
1. After 20 hours user earns TrainingX.AI Certification.
1. $299 Codex Power Bootcamp invite appears.

This is a living platform. It never stops learning the user.

-----

## 18. WHAT YOU (Codex) MUST DO

When working on this repo:

1. **READ THIS FILE FIRST.** Do not skip.
1. **Never hardcode career, trade, or business lists.** Use the agent query schema.
1. **Never violate age gates.** Hard gate at 15.
1. **Never use forbidden language.** Check Section 13.
1. **Always feed every interaction back to the Wristband.** RPCA loop must fire on every click.
1. **Always show salary by zip code.** Required.
1. **Always include businesses under $100.** Required for marginalized communities.
1. **Always show AI credentials FIRST, traditional SECOND.**
1. **Always show familiar roles before new AI roles.**
1. **Cache first. Query second.** Cost control matters.

When in doubt, ASK Tx before acting.

-----

## 19. PUBLIC FACING SCORING RULE

**Locked:** April 28, 2026. Permanent platform rule.

Internal scoring is never exposed to users. Anywhere. Ever.

### What stays internal (never visible in UI or API responses)

- CCIT scores (Clarity, Constraints, Iteration, Tool, individual or combined)
- rpcaScore, promptScore, previousPromptScore
- Invisible Wristband (the term itself, its IDs, its raw fields)
- Digital Thumbprint (the term itself)
- Match algorithm scores, weights, thresholds, formulas
- The score source (whether it came from wristband or userStats)
- Database IDs, internal type fields, raw skill signal numbers

### What is shown to users instead

- "your profile updated"
- "you improved in [skill name]"
- "new matches unlocked"
- "you're [X]% to your next pathway"
- "you earned a certificate"
- "strong match", "growing match", "foundation match" (semantic strength labels, never the raw number)
- Progress bars relative to a next milestone, never an absolute score

### Public copy for the persistent profile

When the user-facing UI needs to describe the system that remembers them, use this exact line and only this line:

"log in once, the system remembers you forever, gets smarter every time you use it"

Show this once, somewhere visible per page that depends on the persistent profile. Never the words "Invisible Wristband" or "Digital Thumbprint" in any user-facing surface.

### Required header on every new UI component

Every new TSX UI component must include this comment block at the top:

```
// INTERNAL SCORING IS NEVER EXPOSED TO USERS. Show outcomes only —
// 'profile updated', 'you improved in X', 'new matches unlocked',
// 'X% to next pathway', 'certificate earned'. Never expose CCIT scores,
// Wristband logic, IDs, formulas, or score sources. Apple-style
// invisible genius. Apply across every page forever.
```

### Scope

This rule binds:

- Every page under `app/`
- Every component under `components/`
- Every Convex query and mutation return value (`convex/`)
- Every agent system prompt and message string (`lib/agents/`)
- Every email template (`convex/emails/`)
- Every PDF, exported document, share card, or certificate body
- Every analytics event payload sent to a third party
- Every future surface yet to be built

### Enforcement

When working in this repo:

1. Read this section before writing any UI or any new API response shape.
2. If a server function is tempted to return `promptScore` or `ccitScores` to the client, refactor it to return an outcome label or progress percentage instead.
3. Audit every existing surface against this rule when touched.
4. If the ask requires showing a score, ask Tx. The default is no.

This rule has no exceptions. It is the same rule for kids, teens, adults, employers, partners, white-label tenants, and admins. Internal scoring is internal forever.

-----

**TrainingX.AI / NuuEDScore LLC | Derrick O'Neal | ORCID: 0009-0004-3282-7042**
**Built on RPCA methodology developed 2012 — before the industry coined "Agentic AI."**

# TrainingX.ai

AI-powered continuous learning platform for prompt engineering and AI skills development.

## Tech Stack

- **Frontend:** Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS
- **Backend:** Convex (serverless backend)
- **Database:** Convex (built-in)
- **AI:** OpenAI API
- **Auth:** Convex Auth (GitHub, Google, Apple, Email/OTP, Password)

## Prerequisites

- Node.js >= 20.9.0
- npm >= 10.8.2
- Convex account (free tier works)

## Quick Start

### 1. Clone and Install

```bash
git clone <repository-url>
cd trainingx
npm install
```

### 2. Set Up Environment Variables

Create `.env.local` file in the root directory:

```bash
NEXT_PUBLIC_CONVEX_URL=https://your-deployment.convex.cloud
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-your-openai-api-key
OPENAI_MODEL=gpt-4o-mini
AI_EVAL_PROVIDER=openai
AUTH_RESEND_KEY=re_your-resend-key
AUTH_EMAIL=onboarding@yourdomain.com
AUTH_TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID=your-twilio-account-sid
AUTH_TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN=your-twilio-auth-token
AUTH_TWILIO_SERVICE_SID=your-twilio-service-sid
AUTH_TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER=+1234567890
AUTH_APPLE_SECRET=your-apple-secret
CONVEX_SITE_URL=https://your-app-domain.com
NEXT_PUBLIC_ELEVENLABS_AGENT_ID=your-elevenlabs-agent-id
NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=http://localhost:3000
```

**Required:**
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_CONVEX_URL` - Get from Convex dashboard
- `OPENAI_API_KEY` - Required for AI features

**Optional:**
- Auth providers (Resend, Twilio, Apple) - Only if using those auth methods
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_ELEVENLABS_AGENT_ID` - Only for voice chat feature

### 3. Set Up Convex

```bash
npx convex dev
```

This will:
- Create a new Convex project (if first time)
- Deploy the schema
- Start the Convex development server

Copy the `NEXT_PUBLIC_CONVEX_URL` from the output to your `.env.local`.

### 4. Seed Database

In Convex Dashboard:
1. Go to Functions tab
2. Find `practiceProjects:seedProjects`
3. Click Run
4. Paste contents of `data/projects-seed.json` as the `projects` argument
5. Click Run

Or use CLI:
```bash
npx convex run practiceProjects:seedProjects --arg projects="$(cat data/projects-seed.json)"
```

### 5. Start Development Server

```bash
npm run dev
```

Open [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000)

## Project Structure

```
trainingx/
├── app/                    # Next.js app router pages
│   └── (routes)/           # Route pages
├── components/             # React components
├── convex/                 # Convex backend functions
│   ├── schema.ts           # Database schema
│   └── users.ts            # User management
├── lib/                    # Shared utilities
├── data/                   # Seed data and configs
└── public/                 # Static assets
```

## Key Features

- **Practice Zone:** Level-based prompt engineering challenges
- **Matching System:** Continuous AI career matching based on skills
- **Success Pathways:** AI career opportunities matched to your profile
- **Certificates:** Auto-issued certifications when requirements met
- **User Stats:** Real-time skill tracking across 11 competencies

## Development

### Running Locally

```bash
npm run dev          # Start Next.js dev server
npx convex dev       # Start Convex backend (in separate terminal)
```

### Building for Production

```bash
npm run build
npm start
```

### Database Seeding

See `QUICK_START.md` for detailed seeding instructions.

## Environment Variables

See `.env.example` (if exists) or the Quick Start section above for all required variables.

## Troubleshooting

### Practice page is empty
- Ensure database is seeded (see Step 4 above)
- Check Convex dashboard for `practiceProjects` table data

### Authentication not working
- Verify `NEXT_PUBLIC_CONVEX_URL` is set correctly
- Check Convex auth configuration in `convex/auth.config.ts`

### AI features not working
- Verify `OPENAI_API_KEY` is set
- Check API key has sufficient credits

## Documentation

- `QUICK_START.md` - Practice zone setup guide
- `README_PRACTICE_SETUP.md` - Practice system details
- `docs/` - Additional documentation

## License

Private - All rights reserved

System Audit & Implementation Report: TrainingX Core Routing Stability
  Date: May 31, 2026
  Scope: Core Onboarding, Auth Persistence, Assessment Routing, Convex Auth, Career Hub Route Guards

  1. Executive Summary
  Core onboarding routing is now stabilized around persisted Convex state instead of legacy browser-only assessment state. The old localStorage["assessment_quiz_results"]
  auto-sync path was removed from active auth routing, preventing new users from being silently marked as completed and sent to legacy /discover/results.

  The active onboarding entry point is now /discover, which renders the new Assessment2165Flow. That flow reads questions from assessment2165:getQuestions, saves partial
  progress to partialAssessments, submits final answers to assessment2165:submit, writes completion flags to users, updates userStats, writes the profile state row, clears
  partial progress, and routes the user to /career-hub.

  2. Root Cause Analysis
  The visible failure had two separate root causes.

  First root cause: legacy results hijack.
  The old results flow used localStorage["assessment_quiz_results"]. If stale legacy results existed in the browser, a newly registered user could be marked as assessment-
  complete without taking the new 25-question assessment. Symptom: user landed on Your AI Readiness Results instead of the new /discover assessment.

  Second root cause: frontend/backend deployment mismatch.
  The staging frontend called assessment2165:getQuestions, but the Convex deployment behind staging did not yet have assessment2165.js:getQuestions deployed. Symptom: client
  crash with Could not find public function for 'assessment2165:getQuestions'.

  3. Architecture & Routing Audit
  Auth source of truth:

  - contexts/AuthContextProvider.tsx reads users.viewer.
  - Auth completion routing now checks user.preAssessmentCompleted.
  - Incomplete users are sent to /discover.
  - Completed users are routed by age lane through getDashboardLaneForAgeGroup.

  Assessment source of truth:

  - New assessment UI: components/assessment/Assessment2165Flow.tsx.
  - New assessment backend: convex/assessment2165.ts.
  - Questions query: assessment2165:getQuestions.
  - Final submit mutation: assessment2165:submit.
  - Partial progress: partialAssessments.savePartialAssessment.
  - Final result persists to users, userStats, profile state row, and quizResults.

  Route guard source of truth:

  - SidebarLayout blocks protected shell until auth and viewer are hydrated.
  - WristbandRouteGuard evaluates access by age lane and allowed surfaces.
  - RouteGuard is still present as a generic protected-route guard, but dashboard shell now primarily gates through SidebarLayout.

  Age lane routing:

  - 8-14 routes to /spiral-the-study-buddy.
  - 15-20 routes to /career-hub.
  - 21-65 routes to /career-hub.
  - Unknown age remains restricted by WristbandRouteGuard on guarded earning/career surfaces.

  4. Technical Changes Verified

  - app/(routes)/(dashboard)/(main)/discover/page.tsx: canonical /discover route renders Assessment2165Flow.
  - components/assessment/Assessment2165Flow.tsx: calls api.assessment2165.getQuestions, saves partial progress, submits via api.assessment2165.submit, redirects to /career-
    hub.
  - convex/assessment2165.ts: implements getQuestions and submit; writes preAssessmentCompleted, assessmentCompleted, assessmentStarted, assessmentProgress, recommendedPath,
    assessmentResults.
  - contexts/AuthContextProvider.tsx: removed legacy offline results sync, routes incomplete users to /discover.
  - app/(routes)/(auth)/signup/page.tsx: after profile completion, users without preAssessmentCompleted go to /discover.
  - app/(routes)/(dashboard)/(main)/discover/results/page.tsx: old legacy results UI removed; route now redirects incomplete users to /discover and completed users to /
    career-hub.
  - components/auth/oauth/SignInWithGoogle.tsx: Google OAuth uses normalized current-origin redirect.
  - lib/auth/appUrl.ts: centralizes app-origin redirect normalization.
  - convex/lib/authRedirect.ts: validates server-side Convex Auth redirect origins.
  - next.config.ts: adds frame-blocking headers for auth routes.

  5. Flow Comparison
  Before:

  - Browser localStorage could override Convex assessment state.
  - New user could skip the new assessment accidentally.
  - /discover/results showed legacy AI Readiness results.
  - Staging frontend could call Convex functions that were not deployed.

  After:

  - New user profile completion sends user to /discover.
  - /discover renders the new 25-question assessment.
  - /discover/results no longer shows legacy results.
  - Convex deployment must include assessment2165.js:getQuestions and assessment2165.js:submit.

  6. Verification Completed

  - npm run typecheck: passed.
  - npx tsx scripts/assessment2165Scoring.test.ts: passed.
  - Convex function check after deploy key usage showed:
      - assessment2165.js:getQuestions
      - assessment2165.js:submit

  7. Remaining Blockers
  Critical:

  - Convex deployment discipline: staging frontend must always point to the same Convex deployment where functions are deployed. Current staging expects quixotic-sturgeon-
    254. If code is pushed to another dev deployment, /discover can crash again.
  - Deploy key rotation: a Convex deploy key was pasted into chat. Rotate it in Convex after this work.

  High:

  - Split source of truth remains: users, userStats, and profile state row are all written. The loop is stabilized, but long-term architecture should define one canonical
    onboarding completion source and make other tables derived.
  - Temporary staging auth bypass exists in lib/auth/stagingBypass.ts. It must stay disabled in production and should be removed after mobile Google auth QA.

  Medium:

  - Destination naming is inconsistent: some decision logic still recommends /ai-database, while adult onboarding now routes to /career-hub. Standardize on Career Hub.
  - ProfileProgressWidget is disabled in app/layout.tsx, while the component still exists with stub pulse logic. Decide whether to delete, rebuild, or re-enable.
  - /auth still has some legacy assessmentStarted logic that can route to /assessment-intro. It should be aligned fully with /discover.

  Incomplete AI-generated / placeholder features:

  - Career Hub still has static or partially generated matching paths in older areas. Confirm Perplexity Sonar Pro live query and cache-first behavior are fully wired before
    calling it complete.
  - Some agent/cache pathways exist but need product QA against the platform rules: salary by zip code, businesses under $100, AI credentials first, familiar roles first.
  - Legacy assessment components still exist under components/assessment/* and data/assessment-questions.ts. They are not the canonical 25-question flow and should be
    quarantined or deleted later.

### 1.2 AuthContextProvider — детальний аналіз

**Файл:** `contexts/AuthContextProvider.tsx` (13 083 байти, оновлено 30.05)

**Що правильно:**
- Видалено legacy `localStorage["assessment_quiz_results"]` sync
- Маршрутизація базується на `user.preAssessmentCompleted` (Convex state)
- `getDashboardLaneForAgeGroup` правильно реалізує вікові ворота: `8-14` → `/spiral-the-study-buddy`, `15-20`/`21-65` → `/career-hub`
- `tx_assessment_completion_bridge` запобігає redirect loop під час hydration (bridge живе 10 хвилин)
- OAuth settling логіка ізольована через `isOAuthCallbackSettling` state

**Проблеми виявлені:**

**P1 — Routing loop ризик у `/auth/page.tsx`:**
```typescript
// auth/page.tsx рядок ~130:
} else if (!assessmentStarted) {
  redirectTo = "/assessment-intro";
}
```
`/auth` перенаправляє на `/assessment-intro`, а не на `/discover`. Але `AuthContextProvider` відправляє неповних користувачів на `/discover`. Це означає: якщо `assessmentStarted === false` але `preAssessmentCompleted !== true`, користувач потрапляє на `/assessment-intro`, а потім `AuthContextProvider` може перекинути його назад на `/discover`. Два різних механізми конкурують.

**P2 — `assessment-intro/page.tsx` — застарілий маршрут:**
Сторінка `/assessment-intro` існує, рендериться через `SidebarLayout`, і кнопка "Start Assessment" викликає `markAssessmentStarted()` + `router.push('/discover')`. Це дублює функціональність. Якщо `/auth` відправляє сюди, а `AuthContextProvider` відправляє на `/discover` — є race condition.

**P3 — `needsProfileCompletion` vs `preAssessmentCompleted` — два прапори:**
```typescript
// AuthContextProvider:
const needsPreAssessment =
  userValue?.needsProfileCompletion !== true &&
  userValue?.preAssessmentCompleted !== true;
```
Логіка: `needsPreAssessment = true` коли ОБИДВА прапори не встановлені. Але `needsProfileCompletion` — це прапор незавершеного профілю (ім'я/вік/локація), а `preAssessmentCompleted` — прапор завершеного assessment. Вони мають різну семантику. Поточна логіка `&&` означає: якщо профіль завершено (`needsProfileCompletion = false`) але assessment не пройдено (`preAssessmentCompleted = false`) — `needsPreAssessment = true`, і користувача відправляють на `/discover`. Це правильно. Але якщо `needsProfileCompletion = true` (профіль не завершено) — `needsPreAssessment = false`, і користувача НЕ відправляють на `/discover`. Це теж правильно (спочатку треба завершити профіль). Логіка коректна, але заплутана.

toolSpecification.name: knowledge
toolSpecification.description:
A tool for indexing and searching content across chat sessions using semantic search.

## Overview
This tool enables persistent storage and retrieval of information using semantic search (MiniLLM) or keyword search (BM25). Content remains available across sessions for later use.

## When to use
- When users ask to query your knowledge bases or kbs
- When you need to search previously indexed content
- When users request to index new content (code, markdown, CSV, PDF, and other text file formats)
- When exploring unfamiliar content to find relevant information
- When users ask about topics that might be in indexed knowledge bases

## When not to use
- When content has not been indexed yet and user hasn't requested indexing
- When you need real-time or external information not in the knowledge base

## Notes
- Use 'show' command to list available knowledge bases before searching
- Search can target specific knowledge bases (context_id) or all knowledge bases
- Use default limit values unless specifically needed; fewer results for focused search
- Pagination available via offset parameter for large result sets
- 'add' command indexes new content; 'update' command refreshes existing knowledge bases
- Unless there is a clear reason to modify the search query, use the user's original wording for better semantic matching

- blocking (default): Waits for all stages to complete, returns consolidated results.

USE THIS when you need multi-step work with specialized agents:
- Research → Implement → Review pipelines
- Parallel research tracks that feed into a single implementer
- Any workflow where stages have dependencies

Each stage becomes a session you can monitor via ctrl+g in the TUI.

toolSpecification.name: write
toolSpecification.description:
A tool for creating and editing text files.

WHEN TO USE THIS TOOL:
- Use when you need to create a new file, or modify an existing file
- Perfect for updating text-based file formats

HOW TO USE:
- Provide the path to the file you want to create or modify
- Specify the operation to perform: one of `create`, `strReplace`, or `insert`
- Use `create` to create a new file. Required parameter is `content`. Parent directories will be created if they are missing.
- Use `strReplace` to replace and update the content of an existing file.
- Use `insert` to insert content at a specific line, or append content to the end of a file.

TIPS:
- To append content to the end of a file, use `insert` with no `insert_line`
